Key suspected bugs per controller: groupByStep/pair occurrence can miscompare repeated same-step read variants on reorder. Let's verify.

`groupByStep` maps step -> traces in actual order. Pairing: expected index i pairs with occurrences[paired] — i.e., actual occurrences in actual order, paired by expected order. For a step with multiple occurrences (same step label repeated), e.g. expected two reads same step "read-x" with different bodies (variant A, variant B), actual has same step twice with variants B, A (reorder). groupByStep actual gives [B, A]. Pairing expected[0]=A with actual[0]=B → body mismatch; expected[1]=B with actual[1]=A → body mismatch. So two spurious body_mismatch findings even though the multiset of reads is identical. That's the contract bug: "Compare independent reads order-insensitively as multiset, do not lose duplicates." Multiset comparison of full trace values, not occurrence-order pairing. So F1 confirmed: same-step repeated read variants miscompared under reorder. Indeed the task says "same-step repeated independent reads multiset (not just distinct step reordering)". Yes.

Also expected duplicate read test uses distinct steps so it doesn't catch.

Also grouping by step and pairing across different kinds: e.g. an expected read step repeated but actual two occurrences where one is mutation? Actually collectTraceDifferences compares. Fine.

Another issue: duplicate step labels across kinds. If expected has read step "x" once and mutation step "x" once, actual has mutation "x" first then read "x". groupByStep actual = [mutation, read]; expected[0] read pairs with actual mutation → kind mismatch etc. That's related F1.

So causal ordering of reads relative to mutations is not checked. Task requires explicit causality dependencies "including causal reads". The RequestTrace doc says "independent reads do not depend on another trace" but reads could have dependencies (causal read). The comparator: for read kind, dependency mismatch is checked (else branch: expected.dependency !== actual.dependency → dependency_mismatch). Wait: for read, the first condition `expected.kind !== "read" && (...)` false, so `else if (expected.dependency !== actual.dependency)` — check dependency equality. So a read with non-null dependency is compared string-equal. But graph order isn't validated: dependency could point to a nonexistent parent, self-cycle, or first mutation with null dependency... Wait mutation null dependency already gives dependency_mismatch only if either is null — but both null → dependency_mismatch (the condition pushes if expected.dependency===null || actual.dependency===null, so both null triggers mismatch too). Actually test "requires an explicit dependency label for mutations" has both null → dependency_mismatch. Good, so missing parent? The contract requires "explicit causality dependencies including causal reads and missing parent/selfcycle/first mutation root contract". Let's parse: task s1-request-comparator line 7: "Mutations/tool/turns require explicit dependency mapping; preserve causal order... Planned model can specify explicit causal step labels". Line 5 of review task: "explicit causality dependencies including causal reads and missing parent/selfcycle/first mutation root contract".

So the comparator does not validate that dependency labels refer to an actually existing step in the same capture (missing parent), does not reject self-dependency (step depends on itself), and does not define a contract for the first mutation root (root-action sentinel? dependency can be null for first mutation if it's the root, but implementation currently flags null dependency on any mutation/tool/turn as dependency_mismatch, and test enshrines that). The task contract may allow "root" explicit label. Hmm, "first mutation root contract" — the first mutation's dependency perhaps should be a root sentinel or explicitly defined. The implementation has no notion of a root; every mutation must have non-null dependency, and dependency is only compared string-only; no check that the referenced step exists or occurs earlier. So deps can point forward in time (a step depends on a later step) and pass — no graph validation. Also causal order only checks filtered sequence of non-reads equals expected sequence, ignoring dependency graph consistency. So a swap of two mutations with different steps is caught by order check, but changing dependency to a nonexistent label that is equal in both captures passes (string-only), i.e., an invalid graph is accepted → false PASS. Also a mutation whose dependency points to itself (step "write-a" dependency "write-a") identical in both captures → no findings → PASS despite self-cycle. So F2/F3.

Also root contract: first mutation with dependency null is reported as dependency_mismatch even when both captures identical, meaning identical captures with a first mutation root → spurious finding, contradicting "identical captures return no differences" and the requirement that first mutation root be accepted? Task says "explicit causality dependencies including ... first mutation root contract". The task s1 says "Mutations/tool/turns require explicit dependency mapping". So explicit mapping could be a root label ("root-action" used in test). The test "matches tool and turn dependencies" uses "root-action" as a label that is not itself a trace. So a root sentinel label allowed but not validated. Hmm, that means dependency labels need not refer to a trace. So "missing parent" check is ambiguous: if root-action sentinel is permitted, then a missing parent can't be distinguished from a root sentinel without a declared root set. The task says "Planned model can specify explicit causal step labels shared across captures rather than volatile requestIDs; document/test chosen contract." The chosen contract in compare.ts says dependency names "the stable label of the causal predecessor" — lines 7-9, and "independent reads do not depend on another trace". If dependency is supposed to name a causal predecessor, then "root-action" in the test is a label with no trace, i.e., missing parent, yet test asserts PASS. That's an internal contract inconsistency: either dependency must name an existing trace (then dependency validation missing) or allow virtual root labels (then must document/validate root sentinel and cannot claim "names the stable label of the causal predecessor"). And no self-cycle detection: step "write-a" dependency "write-a".
